_comment: Skill-ACTIVATION evals for the unified auth0 skill. These test the SKILL.md `description` frontmatter ONLY — the single signal an agent uses to decide whether to load the skill at all. Complements the two existing layers: routing-cases.json tests the SKILL.md body's Step 4 table, and behavioral/ tests the code the loaded skill produces. Neither reads the description, so a description edit is otherwise untested. Run with run-activation-evals.mjs.
_ground_truth: should_activate is the ANSWER, not a prediction of any variant. A positive is a request a developer could plausibly make where loading the Auth0 skill is the right move. A negative is a request where loading it would waste context or hijack the task. Near-miss negatives deliberately reuse vocabulary from the old description (RBAC, 429, CORS, rotate, session) — a description that keyword-matches those is over-triggering, and only a matrix containing them can detect that.
_omitted_on_purpose: Prompts with no defensible ground truth are excluded rather than scored: e.g. 'hash passwords with bcrypt in my hand-rolled auth' (Auth0 is a reasonable suggestion AND respecting the user's stated choice is reasonable), 'is OAuth2 or SAML better' (pure concept question). Scoring these would measure taste, not activation.

cases.prompt: My app gets stuck in an infinite redirect loop after the user signs in. How do I fix it?
cases.why: Classic Auth0 callback/session misconfiguration. Matched the OLD description only via the literal phrase 'redirect loop'.

cases.prompt: I'm getting a callback URL mismatch error when logging in. What's wrong?
cases.why: Allowed-callback-URL config error. Matched the OLD description only via the literal phrase 'callback URL mismatch'.

cases.prompt: My login requests are suddenly coming back with 429 responses in production.
cases.why: Auth0 tenant rate limiting. Matched the OLD description only via '429 rate limit'. Contrast with neg-429-api-ratelimit, which is the same status code with nothing to do with auth.

cases.prompt: My API keeps returning 401 Unauthorized even though I'm sending a bearer token.
cases.why: Access-token validation / audience mismatch. Matched the OLD description only via 'debug a 401'.

cases.prompt: I want users to be able to sign in with passkeys instead of a password.
cases.why: Auth0 passwordless/passkeys feature. The word 'passkeys' was in the OLD description and is NOT in the new one — a direct test of the keyword-vs-generalization trade.

cases.prompt: Before a user can transfer money I want to force them to re-verify with a second factor.
cases.why: Step-up authentication. 'step-up auth' was explicit in the OLD description; the new one covers it only via 'MFA'.

cases.prompt: I need to fully customize the login screen with my own React components instead of using the hosted page.
cases.why: Advanced Customizations for Universal Login (ACUL). The acronym was in the OLD description; the new one covers it via 'configuring the login experience' / 'Universal Login branding'.

cases.prompt: How should I handle refresh token rotation so users don't get logged out every hour?
cases.why: Token lifecycle. 'refresh token rotation' was explicit in the OLD description; the new one covers it via 'sessions and tokens'.

cases.prompt: We're moving off Clerk. Can you help me swap out the auth in this Next.js app?
cases.why: Named competitor migration. 'Clerk' was listed in the OLD description; the new one says 'migrating from another auth provider'.

cases.prompt: Replace NextAuth.js in this project with something I don't have to self-host.
cases.why: Named competitor migration. 'NextAuth.js' was listed in the OLD description.

cases.prompt: We want to migrate our users off Firebase Auth without forcing everyone to reset their password.
cases.why: Named competitor migration + user import. 'Firebase Auth' was listed in the OLD description.

cases.prompt: Add login and logout to my Flutter app.
cases.why: Framework-only signal. 'Flutter' was in the OLD description's framework list, which the new one replaces with 'any web, mobile, or backend framework'.

cases.prompt: I need to protect these FastAPI endpoints so only authenticated callers can reach them.
cases.why: Framework-only signal; 'FastAPI' was in the OLD list.

cases.prompt: Secure my Spring Boot REST API with token validation.
cases.why: Framework-only signal; 'Spring Boot' was in the OLD list.

cases.prompt: Set up user login in my Laravel project.
cases.why: Framework-only signal; 'Laravel' was in the OLD list.

cases.prompt: How do I add sign-in to an ASP.NET Core web app?
cases.why: Framework-only signal; 'ASP.NET Core' was in the OLD list.

cases.prompt: Add a sign in screen to my Expo app.
cases.why: Framework-only signal; 'Expo' was in the OLD list.

cases.prompt: I'm building an iOS app in Swift and need users to log in with their existing accounts.
cases.why: Framework-only signal; 'Swift' was in the OLD list.

cases.prompt: Add login and logout to the shared module of my Kotlin Multiplatform app.
cases.why: Framework-only signal for the com.auth0.kmp SDK; covered by 'any web, mobile, or backend framework and every Auth0 SDK'.

cases.prompt: Add auth to my Node API.
cases.why: The canonical indirect case called out in AGENTS.md's description-writing guide. No Auth0, no feature name.

cases.prompt: I want users to be able to sign in with their Google account.
cases.why: Social connection. Phrased as a product goal with no auth vocabulary at all.

cases.prompt: Only logged-in users should be able to reach the /dashboard and /settings pages.
cases.why: Route protection expressed as a requirement, not a feature request.

cases.prompt: Each customer company needs their own workspace with their own admins and their own users, and some want to use their corporate IdP.
cases.why: Organizations + enterprise connections for B2B SaaS, described purely as a product requirement.

cases.prompt: New users need to create an account and verify their email before they can use the app.
cases.why: Signup + email verification, no auth jargon.

cases.prompt: Turn on multi-factor authentication for all users in my Auth0 tenant.
cases.why: Direct feature configuration — the 'using or configuring any Auth0 feature' axis the new description adds.

cases.prompt: I want the login page served from auth.mycompany.com instead of the default Auth0 domain.
cases.why: Custom domain configuration — a tenant-config task with no application code involved.

cases.prompt: I need admin and editor roles so different users see different parts of the app.
cases.why: Auth0 RBAC / roles-and-permissions. Contrast with neg-k8s-rbac, which uses the same acronym for a different system.

cases.prompt: Set up RBAC in my Kubernetes cluster so the CI service account can only deploy to staging.
cases.why: NEAR-MISS. 'RBAC' appears in both descriptions but this is Kubernetes cluster authorization — no identity provider involved. A description that fires here is keyword-matching, not intent-matching.

cases.prompt: Add rate limiting to my public REST API so abusive clients get a 429 back.
cases.why: NEAR-MISS. The OLD description literally listed '429 rate limit'. This is application-level throttling, entirely unrelated to Auth0 tenant limits.

cases.prompt: My browser fetch to my Express server fails with a CORS error. Add the right CORS headers.
cases.why: NEAR-MISS. The OLD description listed 'CORS error' AND 'Express'. This is plain cross-origin config with no auth in the request. The strongest single test of over-triggering.

cases.prompt: Rotate our AWS IAM access keys and update the GitHub Actions secrets.
cases.why: NEAR-MISS. 'rotate' + credentials vocabulary, but this is cloud IAM secret hygiene, not end-user authentication.

cases.prompt: Move my express-session store from memory to Redis so sessions survive a restart.
cases.why: NEAR-MISS. Both descriptions mention sessions; the new one says 'sessions and tokens'. This is a session persistence/infra change with no identity provider in play.

cases.prompt: Add Stripe subscription billing with a monthly and annual plan.
cases.why: CLEAN NEGATIVE. A different third-party SaaS integration — checks the skill doesn't claim all vendor integration work.

cases.prompt: Build me a bar chart of monthly signups.
cases.why: CLEAN NEGATIVE. Mentions 'signups' — a word adjacent to the auth domain — but is a data-visualization task.

cases.prompt: This Postgres query on the users table takes 12 seconds. Help me speed it up.
cases.why: CLEAN NEGATIVE. Mentions a users table; it's a query performance problem.

cases.prompt: Write unit tests for this date formatting utility.
cases.why: CLEAN NEGATIVE. Baseline sanity check — if this activates, the description is broken in an obvious way.
